checked.ref: observation: suspected defect from item 506 (a bystander's curtain and day boards under a hidden clock)
checked.claim: Suspected, minor to major: transitions.mjs `onClockHeard` starts the curtain's turn hint, the flashes and the day's boards from the clock hooks on every client with no `clockHiddenHere` test, so a bystander may see the clock move during an incident.
checked.why: The road the reader read holds: `registerTransitions` hangs `onClockHeard` on drpgTimeOfDayChanged/drpgPhaseChanged/drpgEclipseChanged; sync.mjs calls those hooks on every client with the world's clock; neither transitions.mjs nor sequence.mjs mentions clockHiddenHere, murderState or the incident (grep), while hud-elapsed.mjs:207 and day-summary.mjs:91 do; clock.mjs:880-889 says the clock moves in private during a murder; eclipse.mjs:185 refuses an Eclipse before Stage 6. But the visible failure is not established. `glass.hintTurn` only sets a hint, which `glassTurn` uses when a recut happens; whether an hour change recuts or recolours a bystander's glass was not traced (the reader says so). Whether a new day or nightfall with a board can be reached during an incident was not traced either. And the question is not new: item 506's own text already says the code reads the clock as it arrives in the browser, so this is the item's question restated with lines, not a new defect. A suspicion with a live check (506's l1), not a finding, and its severity range is not supported.
